subject: Deployment packaging and support holdback — Helix Therapeutics
messages:
From: Linda Park <linda.park@helixtx.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@helixtx.com
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re-evaluating platform fee vs. license mix for Helix pilot

Hi Irene / Marissa —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement had a follow-up ask: given our constrained capital this quarter, would Redwood consider swapping part of the one-time platform fee into an achievement-based holdback tied to onboarding SLAs and uptime?

Specifically:
- We’d like up to 25% of the platform fee to be held and only released after the pilot meets agreed SLA milestones across months 1–3.
- In exchange, we’re asking for a 12% reduction to the upfront platform fee and a one-time onboarding credit of $35k.

Also, we need clarity on operator license counting for our three on-prem sites (staging + 2 prod clusters) — are those counted per physical site or per GPU node? That impacts total cost materially.

Can you share an updated packaging sketch and the SOW redline we can circulate internally? We’re aiming to get procurement approval by end of next week.

Best,
Linda Park\Head of Procurement\Helix Therapeutics

---

On Mon, Jun 7, 2027 at 11:02 AM Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai> wrote:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Linda Park <linda.park@helixtx.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Re-evaluating platform fee vs. license mix for Helix pilot

Hi Linda —

Appreciate the clear ask. We can be flexible, and I pulled together two alternative packaging options (attached: Redwood_Deploy_Pricing_Options_v3.pdf) plus a SOW draft (SOW-Draft-Helix-0607.docx) to make procurement review easier. Short summary below — happy to hop on a 30-min call to walk through.

Option 1 — Platform-first (standard):
- 100% upfront platform fee (amortized over 12 months in accounting)
- Operator licenses counted per active GPU node (standard definition in SOW)
- Full onboarding credit offered: $20k
- Support: Priority SRE band (24x7) included in year 1

Option 2 — Holdback swap (what you asked for):
- Reduce upfront platform fee by 12% (matches your ask)
- Holdback: up to 20% of platform fee held for first 90 days and released upon meeting SLA milestones (availability >= 99.5% and onboarding checklist items 1–6)
- Onboarding credit: $30k applied as invoice credit at go-live
- Support: Year 1 includes Standard SRE band (business hours) + 2x critical incident credits for 24x7 on-call response (billed separately if used)

Notes on operator licenses: our billing counts active inference-serving GPU nodes licensed. If you prefer per-site seat pricing we can model that as an alternative (likely slightly higher for your footprint). I asked Ben to confirm technical amortization and on-prem operator implications below.

Attached: Redwood_Deploy_Pricing_Options_v3.pdf (pricing scenarios), SOW-Draft-Helix-0607.docx (redline-ready).

Next steps I propose:
1) Confirm which option procurement prefers (1 or 2)
2) If Option 2, confirm the exact SLA milestones you want measured and who at Helix will sign-off on the checklist items
3) We’ll finalize SOW and produce a DocuSign link for signature (I’ll include a conditional SLA-credit clause as discussed)

Available for a call Tue/Wednesday — I can book 10–10:30 PT or 2:30–3:30 PT.

Thanks,

Irene Choi\Senior Director, Enterprise Sales\Redwood Inference\Phone: (415) 555-0192

---

On Mon, Jun 7, 2027 at 3:30 PM Linda Park <linda.park@helixtx.com> wrote:
From: Linda Park <linda.park@helixtx.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@helixtx.com
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Re-evaluating platform fee vs. license mix for Helix pilot

Irene —

Thank you for the quick turnaround and the attachments. A few clarifications:
1) The holdback percentage — can we push to 25% (we’re willing to accept the 12% upfront reduction you suggested but want the larger holdback to reduce near-term cash outflow)
2) SLA milestone definition — Helix legal wants objective telemetry-based checks. Can Redwood commit to sending availability metrics to our monitoring workspace for independent verification?
3) Operator license — per GPU node is acceptable, but we need a hard cap for pilot billing so we don’t get surprise overage charges in month 1.

Also, during procurement review they asked whether Redwood would be open to deferring 50% of the Year 1 platform fee for invoices issued in Q3 (two equal invoices: at contract signing and at 90 days) if we accept Option 1 with an extra $15k onboarding credit. That’s another path if holdback creates too much operational overhead for Redwood.

Would appreciate your recommended one-line summary for the CFO to speed approval — we’re on a tight timeline.

Best,
Linda

---

On Tue, Jun 8, 2027 at 10:05 AM Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai> wrote:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Linda Park <linda.park@helixtx.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Re-evaluating platform fee vs. license mix for Helix pilot

Linda / Irene —

Quick tech + commercial note from engineering:
- Operator license = active GPU serving node. For your two prod clusters we recommend capping the pilot at 24 active nodes; we can set a soft cap in the billing engine to prevent surprise consumption charges.
- If Helix can accept the platform fee amortization over two invoices (signing + 90d) we can safely allow the 50% deferment but would ask for a modest markup to cover SRE ramp (we modeled a 3% fee on deferred amount) — I’ll quantify if you want numbers.
- On telemetry: we can stream availability metrics to a read-only workspace in your monitoring account (we’ve done this for two other enterprise customers). That will satisfy objective verification for SLA milestones.

If procurement prefers the larger 25% holdback, engineering is comfortable with the operational design, but we’ll ask for a slightly longer sign-off window (120 days) to avoid disputes on partial milestone completion.

Ben
Principal Sales Engineer\Redwood Inference

---

On Wed, Jun 9, 2027 at 3:42 PM Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai> wrote:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Linda Park <linda.park@helixtx.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, procurement@helixtx.com
Date: Wed, 9 Jun 2027 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Re-evaluating platform fee vs. license mix for Helix pilot

Linda —

Thanks — this is all workable. To put a crisp one-line summary for your CFO: "Redwood offers a pilot-friendly commercial package: 12% upfront platform-fee reduction + conditional holdback tied to objective SLA telemetry, with the option to defer 50% of year-one fees across two invoices if preferred."

Proposal / next steps (pick your path):
- Path A (Holdback): 12% upfront reduction + 25% platform-fee holdback, released on passing telemetry-verified milestones. $30k onboarding credit. SLA sign-off window: 120 days.
- Path B (Defer + Credit): Option 1 with 50% of Year 1 platform fee invoiced at signing and remainder at day-90; $35k onboarding credit. 3% deferment uplift on the deferred amount (to cover SRE ramp).

Additional operational guardrails:
- Billing cap: pilot capped at 24 active GPU serving nodes for month 1.
- Telemetry: we will stream availability metrics into your read-only workspace for independent verification.
- SOW: attached SOW-Draft-Helix-0607.docx includes conditional SLA-credit language; we’ll build the exact milestone list once you confirm which path you prefer.

If you confirm Path A or B in reply I’ll: (a) mark up the SOW accordingly, (b) send a DocuSign link, and (c) calendar a 30-min signature readiness call.

Thanks again — we can hit procurement deadline next Thursday if Helix confirms today or tomorrow.

Regards,
Irene Choi\Senior Director, Enterprise Sales\Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0192

Attachments: Redwood_Deploy_Pricing_Options_v3.pdf, SOW-Draft-Helix-0607.docx
